verdict.rationale: Together AI's own docs cover function/tool calling, parallel function calling, and multi-step and multi-turn tool chaining for building agent loops on its hosted open models. The evidence is all vendor documentation, so the reliability claim ('without breaking') is unverified. missing for 10: independent or hands-on evidence that tool calls are faithful and agent loops don't break, documentation of which models support parallel and multi-step tool use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on faithful function/tool calling — including parallel and multi-step tool use — so agent loops run on open models without breaking

citations.quote: Function calling (also called tool calling) lets LLMs respond with structured function names and arguments that you can execute in your application.
To build agent loops, chain tool calls inside one response (multi-step), and conversations that thread tools across many turns (multi-turn).
Multi-step function calling chains sequential function calls within one conversation turn.
In parallel function calling, the same function is called multiple times simultaneously with different parameters.
